title: High throughput phenotype screening pipeline for functional genomics in Magnaporthe oryzae
protocol: Regeneration of mutants in 24-well plate marks entry into HPS pipeline.
Measure growth of mutants after 3 days on V8 agar, comparing with wild-type.
Score mycelial color visually after 6 days incubation.
Harvest conidia from 6-day old cultures by adding 1 ml Tween 20 solution to each well and rubbing with cotton swab.
Pipette forty-microliters of conidial suspension onto green mirror glass.
Incubate conidial suspension at room temperature for 24 hours.
Observe conidiation, conidial morphology, conidial germination, and appressorium formation under a microscope with x100 magnification.
Score conidiation by comparing the relative number of conidia from mutants to that of wild-type.
Measure the conidial germination rate as the percentage of germinated conidia.
Measure the ability to form appressoria as the percentage of appressorium-forming conidia among the germinated conidia.
Drop conidial suspension onto a green mirror.
Use the remaining conidial suspension for a pathogenicity test.
Spray-innoculate approximately 1000 microliters of spore suspension on rice plants using an artist's airbrush connected to compressed air.
Maintain test tubes in a dew chamber to ensure high humidity required for the fungus to penetrate plant cuticles.
Incubate plants in the dew chamber for 20-24 hours.
Transfer plants to room temperature conditions and keep them there for 3 days.
Assess pathogenicity by visually examining lesions produced on rice plants.
